answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity costly: an agent must lock collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning thousands of fake identities drains the attacker funds instead of multiplying influence. Like a sparrow guarding a single nest in a vast nebula of lookalikes, each verified identity carries a price; when a coordinated swarm hits its nadir of trust, honest agents keep trading while the fakes bleed stake and fade.
